passage: one should not infer that one correlation is greater than the other. (Section on comparing two effects without a direct test: groups of 20 participants; an intervention effect significant in one group but not the other, with equal means but higher variance in one group.)
faulty: improvement = post - pre. One-sample one-sided t test (mean > 0, 0.05) in young and in old participants. HOLDS if significant in young and not significant in old; None if a group has fewer than 2 participants or a zero variance.
fixed: Welch two-sample one-sided t test (0.05) of the improvement of young minus old. HOLDS if p < 0.05; None if a group has fewer than 2 participants or a zero variance.
estimand: Faulty: the pair (young improvement significant, old improvement not). Fixed: the difference in mean improvement between young and old.
model_family: Independent Gaussian improvements per group with group means and group standard deviations; the claim-false world has equal means and unequal standard deviations, as in the source's example.
sizes_note: Source: two groups of 20 participants; 40 participants here. Dependence on size: not stated.
exploited_structure: Two groups whose improvements differ in variability, so the same mean improvement is significant in the less variable group and not in the other.

structure_statistic.note_value_source: source states none: the passage says only that one group has equal means but higher variance; log(2) (a standard-deviation ratio of 2) is proposed
